notes: Phobos Agriculture cooking recipes (Agriculture 0.40.0): what a Hearth-2 turns one portion into. Each recipe takes one item and gives one item of the same mass; cooking adds and removes nothing, and its electricity leaves as room heat. The Hearth-2 draws 2 kW while cooking, so seconds fixes the energy. Published revisions are frozen (frozen-process-recipes.json): change a recipe by adding a revision. A portion in the cooker is cooked by the recipe that names its item, so two recipes may not take the same item.

hearth-potatoes.notes: Hearth revision 1, unchanged since Agriculture 0.2.0: one 0.4 kg portion of raw potatoes into one cooked portion over 90 seconds at 2 kW (0.05 kWh).

hearth-flatbread.notes: Hearth revision 2 (Agriculture 0.41.0): one 0.4 kg portion of wheat grain and one 0.25 kg water ration into one 0.65 kg flatbread over ten minutes at 2 kW (0.33 kWh). The dough is about 62% water to grain, an ordinary bread hydration. The Hearth mills and bakes in one step, and the steam a real loaf loses is not modelled, because the game's air has no water vapour to receive it; the loaf keeps the water's mass.

hearth-soybeans.notes: Hearth revision 3 (Agriculture 0.42.0): one 0.25 kg portion of dry soybeans and one 0.25 kg water ration into one 0.5 kg bowl of soybean stew over fifteen minutes at 2 kW (0.5 kWh). Dry beans take up about their own mass of water when cooked; real soybeans soak for hours first, and the Hearth's short cook is authored. Steam loss is not modelled, so the bowl keeps the water's mass.
